1.w: Better [is] a dry morsel and quietness with it, than a house full of feasting with strife.

2.w: A wise servant rules over a son who acts shamefully, and in the midst of brothers he will share an inheritance.

3.w: The crucible [is] for silver and the furnace for gold, and the One testing hearts [is] YHWH.

4.w: One doing evil pays attention to lips of iniquity; a liar gives ear to a tongue of evil desires.

5.w: One mocking the poor scorns his Maker; one glad at calamity will not be acquitted.

6.w: The crown of old men [are] the sons of sons, and the glory of sons [are] their fathers.

7.w: A lip of excellence is not lovely to a fool, even less to a prince [is] a lip of falsehood.

8.w: A stone of favor [is] a bribe in the eyes of its owners—to all that he turns, he prospers.

9.w: The one covering a transgression is seeking love, and one repeating a word is separating a close friend.

10.w: A rebuke goes down into an understanding one, more than a hundred stripes into a fool.

11.w: An evil one seeks only rebellion, and a cruel messenger will be sent against him.

12.w: Let meet a bear robbed of her cubs with a man, and not a fool in his folly.

13.w: One returning evil in exchange for good—evil shall not depart from his house.

14.w: The beginning of strife [is] a letting out of waters, and before it breaks out, abandon the dispute.

15.w: One justifying the wicked, and condemning the just—even the two of them [are] an abomination to YHWH.

16.w: Why [is] [is] this a payment in the hand of a fool, to buy wisdom without a heart?

17.w: At every time a friend is loving, and a brother is born for distress.

18.w: A man lacking heart is one striking hands, pledging a pledge before the face of his friend.

19.w: The one loving transgression loves strife; the one making high his entrance is seeking destruction.

20.w: The twisted of heart shall not find good, and the turned in his tongue falls into evil.

21.w: The one begetting a fool, grief [is] unto him, and the father of a fool is not glad.

22.w: A joyful heart is good healing, and a spirit stricken dries up the bones.

23.w: A wicked one takes a bribe from the bosom to stretch aside the paths of justice.

24.w: With the face of a discerning one [is] wisdom and the eyes of a fool [are] at the end of the earth.

25.w: A foolish son [is] a grief to his father, and bitterness to her who bore him.

26.w: Surely to fine the righteous [is] not good, to strike nobles for uprightness.

27.w: The one restraining his words [is] one knowing knowledge, [and] calm of spirit [is] a man of understanding.

28.w: Even a fool keeping silent is considered wise, one shutting his lips discerning.
